messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the move catalog and diversify monster learnsets with species-appropriate moves while preserving battle access to learned and monster-stored moves.

## Requirements
- Keep battle access to learned and monster-stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and moves stored on the monster.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles display all available skills.
- Added older/incomplete-record compatibility and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate move, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Validated all 87 species’ learnset entry shapes, skill IDs, and duplicate move IDs.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Finish focused checks for move-pool compatibility, level-up learning, affordability fallback, and enemy fallback.
- Review remaining learnsets for questionable entries.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Rerun the focused script; its enemy-fallback assertion failed because the test monster still had other affordable moves in its pool.
2. Confirm player affordability fallback and enemy fallback with isolated move pools, then review learnsets and run syntax checks.
3. Check `git diff --check` after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species learnsets.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog and eight added moves.
- `src/game/monsters.js`: Monster creation, learnset synchronization, and known move pool.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Player/enemy move selection and affordability behavior.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle move display, attack animations, and HP display timing.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Profile skill display.
- `styles.css`: Battle move-grid styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in the seven listed files.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.
- The last focused check reached the enemy fallback assertion and failed with `0 !== -1`; the test’s enemy retained affordable learnset moves, so isolate its move pool before drawing conclusions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the move catalog and diversify monster learnsets with species-appropriate moves while preserving battle access to learned and monster-stored moves.

## Requirements
- Preserve access to learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaﬀordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Focused checks passed for all 87 learnsets, legacy move pools, level-up/evolution sync, and player/enemy `tackle` fallbacks.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Review remaining learnsets for questionable species/move assignments.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Review remaining learnsets for questionable entries.
2. Rerun syntax checks and `git diff --check` after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species learnsets.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog and eight added moves.
- `src/game/monsters.js`: Monster creation, learnset synchronization, and known move pool.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Player/enemy move selection and affordability behavior.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle move display, attack animations, and HP display timing.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Profile skill display.
- `styles.css`: Battle move-grid styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in seven files: the paths listed above.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

516: export const LEGENDARIES = MONSTER_LIST.filter(m => m.legendary)
517: 
518: export function getMonster(id) {
519:   return MONSTERS[id] || MONSTERS.sprigling
520: }
521: 
522: // Evolution helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
523: export function evolutionOptions(monster, biome = null) {
524:   const species = getMonster(monster.speciesId)
525:   if (!species.evolutions) return []
526:   return species.evolutions.filter(evo => {
527:     switch (evo.type) {
528:       case 'level': return monster.level >= evo.level
529:       case 'item': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1)
530:       case 'friendship': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && monster.friendship >= (evo.friendship || 70)
531:       case 'location': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && (!biome || biome === evo.biome)
532:       default: return false
533:     }
534:   })
535: }
536: 
537: export function baseSpeciesId(speciesId) {
538:   // Walk backwards to the first evolution stage (used by breeding).
539:   let current = getMonster(speciesId)
540:   let guard = 0
541:   while (guard++ < 10) {
542:     const parent = MONSTER_LIST.find(m => m.evolutions.some(e => e.to === current.id))
543:     if (!parent) return current.id
544:     current = parent
545:   }
546:   return current.id
547: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the move catalog and diversify monster learnsets with species-appropriate moves while preserving battle access to learned and stored moves.

## Requirements
- Preserve access to learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaﬀordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Focused checks passed for all 87 learnsets, legacy move pools, level-up/evolution sync, and player/enemy `tackle` fallbacks.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Review remaining learnsets for questionable species/move assignments.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Review remaining learnsets for questionable entries.
2. Rerun syntax checks and `git diff --check` after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species learnsets.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog and eight added moves.
- `src/game/monsters.js`: Monster creation, learnset synchronization, and known move pool.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Player/enemy move selection and affordability behavior.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle move display, attack animations, and HP display timing.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Profile skill display.
- `styles.css`: Battle move-grid styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in seven files: the paths listed above.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.
- The latest review inspected the learnset diff and move definitions; no additional edits or test runs were made.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the move catalog and diversify monster learnsets with species-appropriate moves while preserving battle access to learned and stored moves.

## Requirements
- Preserve access to learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments; no further changes were needed.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species learnsets.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog and eight added moves.
- `src/game/monsters.js`: Monster creation, learnset synchronization, and known move pool.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Player/enemy move selection and affordability behavior.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle move display, attack animations, and HP display timing.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Profile skill display.
- `styles.css`: Battle move-grid styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in seven files: the paths listed above.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster and add secondary types, including types beyond the ones currently represented.
- Preserve the earlier move-catalog, learnset, and battle-access improvements.

## Requirements
- Add more monsters and give monsters secondary typing.
- Introduce additional elements beyond the current set.
- Preserve access to learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments; no further changes were needed.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Plan and implement additional monsters, new elements, and secondary-type support.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Define the new elements and type matchup behavior, then update combat calculations to account for both species types.
2. Update type displays, statistics, and other single-element assumptions for backward compatibility.
3. Add new species with suitable secondary types and verify data references and JavaScript syntax.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog and learnsets; currently 87 species with one `element` each.
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions and battle effectiveness chart.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring use one defender element.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` renders a single element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile and catalog type displays.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Sprite palette is selected from the primary species element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics are counted by the species’ primary element.
- `src/game/world.js`: Wild species are selected from the catalog by biome.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog and eight previously added moves.

## Important Context
- Earlier changes remain uncommitted in seven files: `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

24:   let g = parseInt(hex.slice(3, 5), 16) / 255
25:   let b = parseInt(hex.slice(5, 7), 16) / 255
26:   const max = Math.max(r, g, b), min = Math.min(r, g, b)
27:   let h = 0, s = 0
28:   const l = (max + min) / 2
29:   if (max !== min) {
30:     const d = max - min
31:     s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - max - min) : d / (max + min)
32:     switch (max) {
33:       case r: h = (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0); break
34:       case g: h = (b - r) / d + 2; break
35:       default: h = (r - g) / d + 4
36:     }
37:     h /= 6

## Objective
- Expand the monster roster and add secondary types, including elements beyond the current set, while preserving the existing move catalog, learnsets, and battle-access improvements.

## Requirements
- Add more monsters and give monsters secondary typing.
- Introduce additional elements beyond the current set.
- Preserve access to learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Define additional elements and their matchup behavior; update combat to account for both species types.
- Update type displays, statistics, sprites, and other single-element assumptions compatibly.
- Add species with suitable secondary types and verify data references and JavaScript syntax.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete element definitions and relevant single-element usage.
2. Implement added elements and dual-type effectiveness in combat.
3. Update UI/statistics/rendering for secondary types and add new species.
4. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; currently 87 species with one `element` each.
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions and battle effectiveness chart.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring use one defender element.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` renders a single element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile and catalog type displays.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Sprite palette is selected from the primary species element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics are counted by the species’ primary element.
- `src/game/world.js`: Wild species are selected from the catalog by biome.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog, including eight previously added moves.

## Important Context
- Earlier changes remain uncommitted in seven files: `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.
- `src/data/monsters.js` uses `element` as the primary type; the `M` helper accepts extra properties for species data.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving existing move catalogs, learnsets, battle access, and compatibility with older saves.

## Requirements
- Add more monsters and give monsters secondary types.
- Introduce additional elements and define their matchup behavior.
- Preserve learned and stored move access; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add elements and matchup behavior, then update combat for dual-type effectiveness.
- Update type displays, statistics, sprites, and other single-element assumptions compatibly.
- Add species with suitable secondary types and verify data references and JavaScript syntax.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining element-related assumptions and decide how dual types are represented.
2. Implement additional elements and combine both defender types in battle effectiveness.
3. Update UI/statistics/rendering for secondary types and add new species.
4. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions and battle effectiveness chart.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` helper accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring use one defender element.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile and catalog type displays and filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Sprite palette is selected from the primary species element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the species’ primary element.
- `src/game/world.js`: Wild species are selected from the catalog by biome.
- `src/data/skills.js`: Skill catalog, including eight previously added moves.

## Important Context
- Earlier changes remain uncommitted in seven files: `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Additional single-element assumptions found during inspection include burn immunity in `src/game/battle.js`, element filtering and labels in `src/ui/screens.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older save support.

## Requirements
- Add more monsters and secondary types; define matchup behavior for additional elements.
- Preserve learned and stored move access; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Player HP changes should appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add elements and matchup behavior, then update combat for dual-type effectiveness.
- Update type displays, statistics, sprites, and other single-element assumptions compatibly.
- Add species with suitable secondary types and verify data references and JavaScript syntax.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add the new element definitions and determine how multiple defender types combine for effectiveness.
2. Update battle damage and relevant type-based effects for dual types.
3. Update badges, filters, statistics, sprites, and other displays for secondary types; add species.
4. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring use species elements.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex type displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.

## Important Context
- Earlier changes remain uncommitted in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Additional single-element assumptions include burn immunity and damage/effectiveness in `src/game/battle.js`, codex filtering and labels in `src/ui/screens.js`, catch counters in `src/game/state.js`, and UI labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

20: export function statsOf(monster) {
21:   const sp = getMonster(monster.speciesId)
22:   const level = monster.level
23:   const pers = PERSONALITIES[monster.personality] || PERSONALITIES.hardy
24:   const passive = getPassive(sp.passive)
25:   const stats = {}
26:   for (const key of ['hp', 'atk', 'def', 'spa', 'spd', 'spe']) {
27:     const base = sp.base[key]
28:     let val = key === 'hp'
29:       ? Math.floor(base * (level + 10) / 45) + level + 12
30:       : Math.floor(base * (level + 8) / 50) + 5
31:     if (key !== 'hp') {
32:       if (pers.plus === key) val *= 1.1
33:       if (pers.minus === key) val *= 0.9
34:       if (passive.kind === 'statBoost' && passive.stat === key) val *= passive.value
35:     }
36:     stats[key] = Math.max(1, Math.floor(val))
37:   }
38:   return stats
39: }
40: 
41: export function maxHpOf(monster) {
42:   return statsOf(monster).hp
43: }
44: 
45: export function xpProgress(monster) {
46:   const need = xpNeed(monster.level)
47:   return { current: monster.xp, need, pct: clamp(monster.xp / need, 0, 1) }
48: }

50: function learnsetAt(speciesId, level) {
51:   const sp = getMonster(speciesId)
52:   return sp.learnset.filter(([lvl]) => lvl <= level).map(([, id]) => id)
53: }

55: function unique(arr) { return [...new Set(arr)] }

58:   const sp = getMonster(speciesId)
59:   const lv = clamp(Math.round(level), 1, MAX_LEVEL)
60:   const learned = unique([...learnsetAt(speciesId, lv), ...(opts.extraMoves || []), ...(opts.moves || [])])
61:   let moves = learned.length ? learned : ['tackle']
62:   const personality = opts.personality || pick(PERSONALITY_IDS)
63:   const monster = {
64:     uid: opts.uid || uid('mon'),
65:     speciesId,
66:     nickname: opts.nickname || sp.name,
67:     nicknameCustom: !!opts.nickname,
68:     level: lv,
69:     xp: 0,
70:     personality,
71:     friendship: opts.friendship ?? 35,

79:     caughtNight: !!opts.caughtNight,

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and support for older saves.

## Requirements
- Add monsters and secondary types, with matchup behavior for additional elements.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` when no moves are recorded or when a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Player HP changes should appear after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed for earlier changes.

### Active
- Add new element definitions and matchup behavior, including combining effectiveness across defender types.
- Update battle damage and relevant type-based effects for dual types.
- Update type badges, codex filters, catch statistics, sprites, and other single-element displays; add secondary-type species.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current uncommitted changes before editing.
2. Add element definitions and dual-type effectiveness handling.
3. Apply dual types throughout battle logic, displays, statistics, sprites, and species data while preserving old-save compatibility.
4. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex type displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Additional single-element assumptions include battle burn immunity and effectiveness in `src/game/battle.js`, codex filtering and labels in `src/ui/screens.js`, catch counters in `src/game/state.js`, and labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

526:   return species.evolutions.filter(evo => {

530:       case 'friendship': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && monster.friendship >= (evo.friendship || 70)

537: export function baseSpeciesId(speciesId) {
538:   // Walk backwards to the first evolution stage (used by breeding).
539:   let current = getMonster(speciesId)
540:   let guard = 0

544:     current = parent
545:   }
546:   return current.id

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Apply dual types throughout battle logic, displays, statistics, sprites, and species data.
- Preserve existing uncommitted changes; recent inspection found no edits to `src/data/elements.js` yet.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and combined effectiveness in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Apply dual types to battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Additional single-element assumptions include battle burn immunity and effectiveness in `src/game/battle.js`, codex filtering and labels in `src/ui/screens.js`, catch counters in `src/game/state.js`, and labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Apply dual types throughout battle logic, displays, statistics, sprites, and species data.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and combined effectiveness in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Apply dual types to battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Recent inspection found no edits to `src/data/elements.js` yet.
- Additional single-element assumptions include battle burn immunity and effectiveness in `src/game/battle.js`, codex filtering and labels in `src/ui/screens.js`, catch counters in `src/game/state.js`, and labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Apply dual types throughout battle logic, displays, statistics, sprites, and species data.
- Support dual-type badges, codex filtering, and element-based catch statistics.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and combined effectiveness in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and apply them to battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.

22: function hexToHsl(hex) {
23:   let r = parseInt(hex.slice(1, 3), 16) / 255
24:   let g = parseInt(hex.slice(3, 5), 16) / 255
25:   let b = parseInt(hex.slice(5, 7), 16) / 255
26:   const max = Math.max(r, g, b), min = Math.min(r, g, b)
27:   let h = 0, s = 0
28:   const l = (max + min) / 2
29:   if (max !== min) {
30:     const d = max - min
31:     s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - max - min) : d / (max + min)
32:     switch (max) {
33:       case r: h = (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0); break
34:       case g: h = (b - r) / d + 2; break
35:       default: h = (r - g) / d + 4
36:     }
37:     h /= 6
38:   }
39:   return [h * 360, s * 100, l * 100]
40: }

43:   const [h, s, l] = hexToHsl(hex)
44:   return `hsl(${(h + hue + 360) % 360} ${Math.max(0, Math.min(100, s + sat))}% ${Math.max(4, Math.min(96, l + light))}%)`

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and apply them to battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
- Recent inspection confirmed current skills and elements use the existing nine element IDs; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects to support them.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`; recent inspection did not modify files.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

22: function hexToHsl(hex) {
23:   let r = parseInt(hex.slice(1, 3), 16) / 255
24:   let g = parseInt(hex.slice(3, 5), 16) / 255
25:   let b = parseInt(hex.slice(5, 7), 16) / 255
26:   const max = Math.max(r, g, b), min = Math.min(r, g, b)
27:   let h = 0, s = 0
28:   const l = (max + min) / 2
29:   if (max !== min) {
30:     const d = max - min
31:     s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - max - min) : d / (max + min)
32:     switch (max) {
33:       case r: h = (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0); break
34:       case g: h = (b - r) / d + 2; break
35:       default: h = (r - g) / d + 4
36:     }
37:     h /= 6
38:   }
39:   return [h * 360, s * 100, l * 100]
40: }

42: function tint(hex, hue = 0, sat = 0, light = 0) {

## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Current skills use the existing nine element IDs: `none`, `nature`, `flame`, `frost`, `earth`, `shadow`, `light`, `storm`, and `dragon`; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.

## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Current skills use the existing nine element IDs: `none`, `nature`, `flame`, `frost`, `earth`, `shadow`, `light`, `storm`, and `dragon`; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Current skill elements are the existing nine IDs: `none`, `nature`, `flame`, `frost`, `earth`, `shadow`, `light`, `storm`, and `dragon`; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

22: function hexToHsl(hex) {
23:   let r = parseInt(hex.slice(1, 3), 16) / 255
24:   let g = parseInt(hex.slice(3, 5), 16) / 255
25:   let b = parseInt(hex.slice(5, 7), 16) / 255
26:   const max = Math.max(r, g, b), min = Math.min(r, g, b)
27:   let h = 0, s = 0
28:   const l = (max + min) / 2
29:   if (max !== min) {
30:     const d = max - min
31:     s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - max - min) : d / (max + min)
32:     switch (max) {
33:       case r: h = (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0); break
34:       case g: h = (b - r) / d + 2; break
35:       default: h = (r - g) / d + 4
36:     }
37:     h /= 6
38:   }
39:   return [h * 360, s * 100, l * 100]
40: }

42: function tint(hex, hue = 0, sat = 0, light = 0) {
43:   const [h, s, l] = hexToHsl(hex)
44:   return `hsl(${(h + hue + 360) % 360} ${Math.max(0, Math.min(100, s + sat))}% ${Math.max(4, Math.min(96, l + light))}%)`
45: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Current skill elements are `none`, `nature`, `flame`, `frost`, `earth`, `shadow`, `light`, `storm`, and `dragon`; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.

13: // stages -6..6 → multiplier
14: function stageMultiplier(stage) {
15:   return stage >= 0 ? (2 + stage) / 2 : 2 / (2 - stage)
16: }

18: function stageName(stage) {

21:   if (stage >= 3) return 'sharply rose'

28: export class Battle {
29:   constructor({ state, enemies, trainer = null, source = { kind: 'wild' }, biome = 'forest' }) {
30:     this.state = state
31:     this.enemies = enemies.filter(Boolean)
32:     this.trainer = trainer
33:     this.source = source
34:     this.biome = biome
35:     this.kind = source.kind
36:     this.isWild = this.kind === 'wild'

39:     this.playerParty = state.party.filter(m => !m.isEgg)
40:     this.activeIndex = this.playerParty.findIndex(m => m.hp > 0)
41:     this.enemyIndex = this.enemies.findIndex(m => m.hp > 0)
42:     this.stages = { player: this.blankStages(), enemy: this.blankStages() }
43:     this.energy = { player: new Map(), enemy: new Map() }
44:     for (const m of this.playerParty) this.energy.player.set(m.uid, 100)
45:     for (const m of this.enemies) this.energy.enemy.set(m.uid, 100)
46:     this.seeded = { player: false, enemy: false }
47:     this.turn = 0
48:     this.over = false
49:     this.result = null

51:     this.participants = new Set()
52:     this.events = []
53:     this.rewards = { money: 0, trainerXp: 0, items: [] }
54:     this.caughtMonster = null
55:     this.playerName = state.player.name
56:     if (this.activeIndex < 0) this.activeIndex = 0

58:     this.addParticipant()
59:   }
60: 
61:   blankStages() { return { atk: 0, def: 0, spa: 0, spd: 0, spe: 0, acc: 0 } }
62: 
63:   get active() { return this.playerParty[this.activeIndex] }
64:   get enemy() { return this.enemies[this.enemyIndex] }
65:   get activeStats() { return statsOf(this.active) }
66:   get enemyStats() { return statsOf(this.enemy) }
67:   get activeEnergy() { return this.energy.player.get(this.active?.uid) ?? 100 }
68:   set activeEnergy(v) { this.energy.player.set(this.active.uid, clamp(v, 0, 100)) }

72:   log(text) { this.events.push({ type: 'log', text }) }
73: 
74:   hpEvent(side, extra = {}) {
75:     const m = side === 'player' ? this.active : this.enemy
76:     this.events.push({ type: 'hp', side, hp: m.hp, maxHp: maxHpOf(m), ...extra })
77:   }

80:     this.events = []
81:     const e = this.enemy
82:     const p = this.active
83:     if (this.trainer) {
84:       this.log(`${this.trainer.name} challenges you!`)
85:       this.log(`${this.trainer.name} sent out ${e.nickname}!`)
86:     } else if (this.kind === 'boss' || this.kind === 'mythic') {
87:       this.log(`${this.source.entity?.name || getMonster(e.speciesId).name} blocks your path!`)
88:     } else {
89:       this.log(`A wild ${getMonster(e.speciesId).name} appeared!`)
90:     }
91:     this.log(`Go, ${p.nickname}!`)
92:     // on-entry passives
93:     this.onEntry('enemy', 'player')
94:     this.onEntry('player', 'enemy')
95:     return this.events
96:   }
97: 
98:   onEntry(side, foeSide) {
99:     const m = side === 'player' ? this.active : this.enemy
100:     const sp = getMonster(m.speciesId)
101:     const passive = getPassive(sp.passive)
102:     if (passive.kind === 'onEntry') {
103:       this.applyStage(foeSide, passive.stat, passive.stages, `${getMonster(this[foeSide === 'player' ? 'active' : 'enemy'].speciesId).name}`)
104:       this.log(`${getMonster(m.speciesId).name}'s ${passive.name} ${stageName(passive.stages)} the foe's ${passive.stat.toUpperCase()}!`)
105:     }

107: 
108:   addParticipant() {
109:     if (this.active) this.participants.add(this.active.uid)

111: 
112:   stageOf(side, stat) { return this.stages[side][stat] || 0 }
113: 
114:   applyStage(side, stat, stages, label) {
115:     if (!stat || !(stat in this.stages[side])) return
116:     this.stages[side][stat] = clamp(this.stages[side][stat] + stages, -6, 6)
117:   }
118: 
119:   statValue(side, stat) {
120:     const m = side === 'player' ? this.active : this.enemy
121:     const stats = statsOf(m)
122:     let value = stats[stat] || 1
123:     if (stat !== 'hp') value *= stageMultiplier(this.stageOf(side, stat))
124:     if (stat === 'atk' && m.status === 'burn') value *= 0.5
125:     if (stat === 'spe' && m.status === 'paralysis') value *= 0.5
126:     return Math.max(1, value)
127:   }

129:   // ── player actions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130:   takeTurn(action) {
131:     if (this.over) return { events: [], over: true, result: this.result }
132:     if (this.awaitingSwitch) return { events: [], awaitingSwitch: true }
133:     this.events = []
134:     this.turn++
135: 
136:     if (action.type === 'switch') return this.doSwitchTurn(action.index)
137:     if (action.type === 'item') return this.doItemTurn(action)
138:     if (action.type === 'capture') return this.doCaptureTurn(action)
139:     if (action.type === 'escape') return this.doEscapeTurn()

142:   }
143: 
144:   doMoveTurn(index) {
145:     const selectedPlayerMove = knownMovePool(this.active)[index] || getSkill('tackle')
146:     const playerMove = selectedPlayerMove.cost <= this.activeEnergy ? selectedPlayerMove : getSkill('tackle')
147:     const enemyMove = this.chooseEnemyMove()
148:     const playerPriority = playerMove.priority || 0
149:     const enemyPriority = enemyMove.priority || 0
150:     const playerSpeed = this.statValue('player', 'spe')
151:     const enemySpeed = this.statValue('enemy', 'spe')
152:     const playerFirst = playerPriority > enemyPriority || (playerPriority === enemyPriority && (playerSpeed > enemySpeed || (playerSpeed === enemySpeed && Math.random() < 0.5)))
153: 
154:     const order = playerFirst ? ['player', 'enemy'] : ['enemy', 'player']
155:     for (const side of order) {
156:       if (this.over) break
157:       if (side === 'player' && this.active.hp <= 0) continue
158:       if (side === 'enemy' && this.enemy.hp <= 0) continue
159:       if (side === 'player') this.useMove('player', index)

161:       const faints = this.checkFaints()

164:     if (!this.over) this.endOfTurn()

166:   }

169:     const m = this.playerParty[index]

171:       this.log('That monster cannot battle right now.')
172:       return { events: this.events, over: false, rejected: true }
173:     }
174:     this.switchPlayer(index, true)
175:     const enemyMove = this.chooseEnemyMove()
176:     if (!this.over) this.useMove('enemy', enemyMove.index)
177:     this.checkFaints()
178:     if (!this.over) this.endOfTurn()
179:     return this.finishTurnEvents()
180:   }
181: 
182:   doItemTurn(action) {
183:     const result = this.useBattleItem(action.itemId, action.targetIndex)
184:     if (result?.fled) return this.finishTurnEvents()
185:     if (!this.over) {
186:       const enemyMove = this.chooseEnemyMove()
187:       this.useMove('enemy', enemyMove.index)
188:       this.checkFaints()
189:     }
190:     if (!this.over) this.endOfTurn()
191:     return this.finishTurnEvents()
192:   }
193: 
194:   doCaptureTurn(action) {
195:     const item = getItem(action.itemId)
196:     if (!this.canCapture) { this.log('You cannot capture another trainer\'s monster!'); return { events: this.events, over: false, rejected: true } }
197:     if (item.type !== 'orb') return { events: this.events, over: false, rejected: true }
198:     if ((this.state.inventory[action.itemId] || 0) <= 0) { this.log(`You are out of ${item.name}.`); return { events: this.events, over: false, rejected: true } }

213:       caught.caughtAt = Date.now()
214:       caught.caughtBiome = this.biome

216:       recordCatch(this.state, caught, { night: caught.caughtNight })
217:       const toParty = addMonster(this.state, caught)
218:       this.caughtMonster = caught

221:       this.result = 'caught'

223:       this.state.stats.battles++
224:       return this.finishTurnEvents()
225:     }
226:     this.log('Oh no! The monster broke free!')
227:     this.events.push({ type: 'capture-fail' })
228:     const enemyMove = this.chooseEnemyMove()
229:     if (!this.over) this.useMove('enemy', enemyMove.index)
230:     this.checkFaints()
231:     if (!this.over) this.endOfTurn()
232:     return this.finishTurnEvents()
233:   }
234: 
235:   doEscapeTurn() {
236:     if (!this.canEscape) {
237:       this.log('There is no running from this battle!')
238:       return { events: this.events, over: false, rejected: true }
239:     }
240:     const ps = statsOf(this.active).spe
241:     const es = statsOf(this.enemy).spe
242:     const chance = clamp(0.5 + (ps - es) / 160, 0.25, 0.95)
243:     if (Math.random() < chance) {
244:       this.log('You got away safely!')
245:       this.result = 'escaped'
246:       this.over = true
247:       this.state.stats.battles++
248:       this.events.push({ type: 'escaped' })
249:       return this.finishTurnEvents()
250:     }

252:     this.events.push({ type: 'escape-fail' })
253:     const enemyMove = this.chooseEnemyMove()
254:     this.useMove('enemy', enemyMove.index)
255:     this.checkFaints()

523: export function evolutionOptions(monster, biome = null) {
524:   const species = getMonster(monster.speciesId)
525:   if (!species.evolutions) return []
526:   return species.evolutions.filter(evo => {
527:     switch (evo.type) {
528:       case 'level': return monster.level >= evo.level
529:       case 'item': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1)
530:       case 'friendship': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && monster.friendship >= (evo.friendship || 70)
531:       case 'location': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && (!biome || biome === evo.biome)
532:       default: return false
533:     }
534:   })
535: }

537: export function baseSpeciesId(speciesId) {
538:   // Walk backwards to the first evolution stage (used by breeding).
539:   let current = getMonster(speciesId)
540:   let guard = 0
541:   while (guard++ < 10) {
542:     const parent = MONSTER_LIST.find(m => m.evolutions.some(e => e.to === current.id))
543:     if (!parent) return current.id
544:     current = parent
545:   }
546:   return current.id
547: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the monster roster with secondary types and new elements while preserving move access, battle compatibility, and older-save support.
- Combine effectiveness across dual-type defenders and synchronize displayed HP changes with attack animations.

## Requirements
- Add new elements, dual-type species, and matchup behavior that combines effectiveness across defender types.
- Preserve learned and stored moves; use `tackle` if no moves are recorded or a move is unaffordable.
- Maintain compatibility with older or incomplete save records.
- Display player HP changes after the corresponding attack animation.

## Decisions
- Battle move pools combine learned moves and stored moves.
- Unaffordable player moves fall back to `tackle`; enemy fallback uses `tackle` with index `-1`.
- Battle UI tracks displayed HP from events so HP changes align with attack animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the four-move cap and equipped-move controls; profiles show all available skills.
- Added compatibility for older/incomplete records and a scrollable battle move grid.
- Added eight catalog moves and diversified learnsets; corrected Celestag’s duplicate, Tombwarden’s malformed entry, and Dracoil’s move.
- Checked all 87 learnsets for unknown or duplicate skills and reviewed new species/move assignments.
- Earlier JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Add element definitions and combined dual-type effectiveness.
- Assign secondary types and update battle logic, species, UI displays and filters, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.

### Blocked
- No test files or `package.json` were found, so no project test suite is available.

## Next Move
1. Add element definitions and a combined dual-type effectiveness helper in `src/data/elements.js`.
2. Assign secondary types and update battle checks, labels, badges, codex filtering, catch statistics, sprites, and element-based effects.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/elements.js`: Element definitions, matchup chart, and `effectiveness()`.
- `src/data/monsters.js`: Species catalog; `M` accepts extra species properties.
- `src/game/battle.js`: Damage, immunity, burn immunity, effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- `src/ui/common.js`: `elementBadge()` currently renders one element.
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Monster profile, codex displays, and element filtering.
- `src/render/sprites.js`: Palette and wing styling currently use the primary element.
- `src/game/state.js`: Catch statistics count the primary element.
- `src/game/progress.js`: Element catch objectives read `catchesByElement`.
- `src/app.js`: Starter, guardian, evolution, and other element displays.
- `src/ui/battleUI.js`: Battle metadata and caught-monster element displays.
- `styles.css`: Element badge styles.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes are present in `src/data/monsters.js`, `src/data/skills.js`, `src/game/monsters.js`, `src/game/battle.js`, `src/ui/battleUI.js`, `src/ui/screens.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Current skill elements are `none`, `nature`, `flame`, `frost`, `earth`, `shadow`, `light`, `storm`, and `dragon`; no element or dual-type edits have been made yet.
- `src/game/battle.js` currently checks only `getMonster(...).element` for burn immunity, damage effectiveness, and enemy move scoring.
- Codex filtering in `src/ui/screens.js`, labels in `src/app.js` and `src/ui/battleUI.js`, palettes in `src/render/sprites.js`, and catch counters in `src/game/state.js` also assume one element.
- New learnset entries affect new monsters immediately; existing monsters receive newly eligible moves through `syncLearned`, such as on level-up or evolution.
